title: Bloom Filters
interviewAnswer: A Bloom filter is a compact probabilistic set-membership structure: it can return false positives but not false negatives under normal insert/query use.
why: Bloom filters avoid expensive storage/cache lookups when a key definitely is absent.
intuition: They answer “definitely not present” or “maybe present.”
deepDive: Each inserted key sets k hash-selected bits; queries test those bits. Saturation raises false-positive probability.
commonMistakes: Saying Bloom filters have false negatives by design.
Deleting from a standard Bloom filter without a counting variant.
followUps: How do k and array size affect false positives?
production: Size for expected cardinality and monitor saturation.
workedExample: A storage engine can skip disk reads for keys the filter says are absent.
